newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army sex scandal not an "epidemic" - Cohen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army sex scandal not an "epidemic" - Cohen.

text.p: Defence Secretary Willian Cohen said on Tuesday that high-profile cases of sexual harassment and marital cheating in the U.S. military were not an epidemic, and praised the armed forces for dealing with the matter openly.
"I'm not worried that it's an epidemic. I think we're going through a period in which this has become very much in high profile," Cohen told reporters.
"I believe overall our military is doing an outstanding job, our leaders are doing an outstanding job and we are dealing with the issue in a very proactive and open fashion."
Cohen responded to questions from reporters shortly after the Army said that the commanding general of its scandal-plagued Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maj. Gen. John Longhouser, was retiring.
One defence official privately confirmed a New York Times report that Longhouser admitted to previously having an adulterous affair.

"We expect the highest of standards from our military leaders. They fully understand that and this individual is retiring based upon his belief that it is in the best interests of the Army," Cohen said.
"So these happen from time to time, but I think that it's the appropriate thing to do."

In addition to a major scandal involving harassment and rape of young female recruits by Army drill sergeants, Longhouser became the latest in a recent series of military officers to be relieved of their duties or required to leave the service because of alleged martial infidelity.

The Navy said last week it had relieved Rear Adm. R. M. Mitchell Jr. of his duties as commander of the Navy Supply Systems Command at Mechanicsburg, Pa., because of allegaions of conduct unbecoming an officer. A defence source said he was accused of making advances toward a subordinate.
